title: The Great Flood
excerpt: God tells Noah, “Enter the ark, you and all your household, for you alone I have found righteous in this generation” (7:1). Seven pairs of every clean animal and one pair of every unclean animal are to be loaded, plus seven pairs of birds. The Lord warns that in seven days He will send rain for forty days and nights. Noah does exactly what he is told. At age 600, Noah leads his wife, his three sons, and their wives into the ark. Animals arrive “two by two” as God brings them. After the family and creatures are inside, they wait seven days; then the floodwaters begin. On the seventeenth day of the second month, “all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened” (7:11). Rain falls for forty days. Noah’s family and every breathing creature are safe inside. “Then the LORD shut him in” (7:16), sealing the ark from the outside. For forty days the waters rise, lifting the ark. Eventually—even the highest mountains are covered by fifteen cubits of water. Every air-breathing creature on land dies. “Only Noah and those with him in the ark remained” (7:23). The waters dominate the earth for 150 days.In this dramatic chapter of Genesis, we witness the execution of God's judgment on a corrupt world through a great flood. Amid the chaos, Noah's family and a selected group of animals find refuge in an ark, highlighting the mercy of God amidst His judgement, and the importance of faith and obedience.

people.name: Noah
people.description: Described as a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked faithfully with God. Noah is the central human figure in the flood narrative, chosen by God to build the ark and preserve life. The Hebrew name "Noah" (נֹחַ, Noach) means "rest" or "comfort."

people.name: Noah's Wife
people.description: Although not named in the text, she is mentioned as accompanying Noah into the ark. Her role is significant as part of the family unit that God preserved.

people.name: Shem
people.description: One of Noah's three sons, Shem is often associated with the Semitic peoples. His name in Hebrew (שֵׁם, Shem) means "name" or "renown."

people.name: Ham
people.description: Another son of Noah, Ham is traditionally linked to the peoples of Africa and parts of the Near East. His name in Hebrew (חָם, Cham) is often associated with "hot" or "warm."

people.name: Japheth
people.description: The third son of Noah, Japheth is traditionally associated with the peoples of Europe and parts of Asia. His name in Hebrew (יֶפֶת, Yepheth) is thought to mean "expansion" or "enlargement."

people.name: Shem's Wife
people.description: Like Noah's wife, she is not named in the text but is included as part of the family entering the ark.

people.name: Ham's Wife
people.description: Also unnamed, she is part of the family group that God saves through the flood.

people.name: Japheth's Wife
people.description: The final member of Noah's family mentioned in the text, she too is unnamed but included in the group entering the ark.

place.name: The Ark
place.description: While not a geographical location, the Ark is a significant place in Genesis 7. It is the vessel that Noah built according to God's instructions to save his family and pairs of every living creature from the Flood. The Hebrew word for "ark" is "תֵּבָה" (tevah), which signifies a large, box-like structure.

place.name: The Earth
place.description: The entire Earth is a central focus in Genesis 7, as it is the location that experiences the Flood. The Hebrew word for "earth" is "אֶרֶץ" (eretz), which can mean land, country, or the whole world, depending on the context. In this chapter, it refers to the entire inhabited world that was covered by the waters of the Flood.

place.name: The Heavens
place.description: The "heavens" are mentioned in the context of the rain that falls for forty days and forty nights. The Hebrew word "שָׁמַיִם" (shamayim) is used, which can mean the sky or the abode of God. In Genesis 7, it refers to the sky from which the rain descends.

events.name: God Commands Noah to Enter the Ark
events.description: God instructs Noah to enter the ark with his family and the animals. The Lord says to Noah, "Go into the ark, you and your whole family, because I have found you righteous in this generation" (Genesis 7:1). The Hebrew word for "righteous" is צַדִּיק (tzaddik), indicating Noah's moral integrity and faithfulness.

events.name: Gathering of Animals
events.description: Noah is commanded to take seven pairs of every kind of clean animal and one pair of every kind of unclean animal, along with seven pairs of every kind of bird, to keep their various kinds alive throughout the earth (Genesis 7:2-3). The distinction between "clean" (טָהוֹר, tahor) and "unclean" (טָמֵא, tamei) animals is significant in the Hebrew context, relating to later dietary laws.

events.name: Seven Days Until the Flood
events.description: God informs Noah that in seven days, He will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and He will wipe from the face of the earth every living creature He has made (Genesis 7:4). The number seven often symbolizes completeness or divine perfection in Hebrew culture.

events.name: Noah's Obedience
events.description: Noah does everything that the Lord commands him (Genesis 7:5). This obedience is a recurring theme in the narrative, emphasizing Noah's faith and trust in God's instructions.

events.name: Noah and His Family Enter the Ark
events.description: Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives enter the ark to escape the waters of the flood (Genesis 7:7). This act of entering the ark signifies their faith in God's promise of salvation.

events.name: Animals Enter the Ark
events.description: Pairs of clean and unclean animals, birds, and creatures that move along the ground, male and female, come to Noah and enter the ark as God had commanded (Genesis 7:8-9). The phrase "as God had commanded" underscores the divine orchestration of events.

events.name: The Flood Begins
events.description: After seven days, the floodwaters come upon the earth. In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the springs of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened (Genesis 7:10-11). The Hebrew term for "floodgates" (אֲרֻבּוֹת, arubot) suggests a deluge of cosmic proportions.

events.name: Forty Days and Nights of Rain
events.description: Rain falls on the earth for forty days and forty nights (Genesis 7:12). The number forty often represents a period of testing or judgment in biblical literature.

events.name: The Ark is Sealed
events.description: On the very day that Noah and his family enter the ark, the Lord shuts them in (Genesis 7:16). This act of God sealing the ark signifies divine protection and the finality of His judgment.

events.name: The Floodwaters Increase
events.description: The floodwaters increase greatly on the earth, and the ark floats on the surface of the water (Genesis 7:18). The rising waters symbolize the overwhelming nature of God's judgment.

events.name: The Earth is Covered
events.description: The waters rise and cover the mountains to a depth of more than fifteen cubits (Genesis 7:20). This complete submersion indicates the totality of the flood's impact.

events.name: Destruction of All Life
events.description: Every living thing that moved on the earth perishes—birds, livestock, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all mankind (Genesis 7:21). The Hebrew word for "perish" (גָּוַע, gava) conveys the finality of the destruction.

events.name: Only Noah Remains
events.description: Only Noah and those with him in the ark survive (Genesis 7:23). This preservation highlights God's faithfulness to His covenant with Noah.

events.name: Floodwaters Prevail for 150 Days
events.description: The waters prevail upon the earth for 150 days (Genesis 7:24). This extended period emphasizes the severity and completeness of the flood judgment.
